frozen_original.title: Kash Patel FBI Purges 30% of Counterintelligence Division — Replaces With Loyalists
frozen_original.synopsis: Following his confirmation as FBI Director in early 2025, Kash Patel initiated a sweeping purge of the FBI's senior leadership, with reports indicating that approximately 30% of the counterintelligence division was replaced, reassigned, or forced out. Career agents and analysts who had worked on Russia, China, and domestic terrorism investigations were targeted. Patel filled senior positions with loyalists who had no relevant experience or whose primary qualification was personal loyalty to Trump. Former intelligence officials and national security experts warned the purge was gutting the FBI's counterintelligence capabilities at a time of acute foreign threats, and that the replacements left critical intelligence gaps that adversaries could exploit.

frozen_original.title: Trump Calls Immigrants 'Animals' at California Roundtable
frozen_original.synopsis: At a May 16, 2018 White House roundtable on sanctuary cities, as a Fresno County sheriff described the difficulty of removing gang members, Trump responded by saying 'We have people coming into the country — or trying to come in — and we're stopping a lot of them, but we're taking people out of the country. You wouldn't believe how bad these people are. These aren't people. These are animals.' While the White House initially claimed Trump was referring specifically to MS-13, the full transcript and context showed the comment was made broadly about immigrants. Using the word 'animals' to describe human beings echoes historical dehumanization rhetoric used to justify atrocities and was condemned by human rights organizations worldwide.

primary.title: Trump Uses “Animals” Remark During California Immigration Roundtable
primary.description_short: Trump Used “Animals” Remark During May 2018 California Immigration Roundtable
primary.description_medium: At a May 16, 2018, White House roundtable on sanctuary-city policies, President Donald Trump said, “These aren’t people. These are animals” after Fresno County Sheriff Margaret Mims said she knew of an MS-13 member she could not report to ICE. Trump’s reply referred broadly to “people coming into the country” without naming a group. The White House and Trump later said he meant MS-13; FactCheck.org said the original remark’s intended target could not be established with certainty.
primary.description_long: On May 16, 2018, President Donald Trump held a White House roundtable with California mayors, sheriffs and other officials about sanctuary-city policies. During the discussion, Fresno County Sheriff Margaret Mims said she knew of an MS-13 member but could not tell ICE unless that person met a threshold. Trump replied that “people coming into the country” were “animals,” saying, “These aren’t people. These are animals.” In the official transcript, the remark immediately follows Mims’s reference to MS-13, but Trump’s reply does not name the gang. The White House press secretary later said Trump was referring to MS-13 gang members, and Trump said the next day that he meant MS-13. FactCheck.org reported those explanations while noting that it could not determine exactly what Trump meant in the original remark. The record should therefore describe the words and their immediate setting, then attribute the later clarification separately. It should not say the transcript proves that Trump was referring to all immigrants, or that it definitively proves he meant only MS-13. The sources establish the public remark and context; they do not document a resulting policy change or quantify harm caused by it.

evidence_map.source_excerpt: Later that day, White House Press Secretary Sarah Sanders was asked what the president meant by the remark, and she said he “was very clearly referring to MS-13 gang members.” Later that same day, Trump, too, was asked to clarify his remarks.

evidence_map.fact: Trump's reply referred to 'people coming into the country' without naming a group in that phrase.
evidence_map.quote: people coming into the country, or trying to come in
evidence_map.source_excerpt: THE PRESIDENT: We have people coming into the country, or trying to come in — and we’re stopping a lot of them.

evidence_map.fact: Trump clarified the next day that he was referring to MS-13 gangs.
evidence_map.quote: But I’m referring, and you know I’m referring, to the MS-13 gangs that are coming in.
evidence_map.source_excerpt: Later that same day, Trump, too, was asked to clarify his remarks, and he said: “But I’m referring, and you know I’m referring, to the MS-13 gangs that are coming in.”
